items.finding: CCPU include and local accessor declarations
items.evidence: cpu4gen.h declares c_setLDT_BASE_LIMIT as IBOOL; c_reg.c:1686 implements VOID. Local extern int repeats header mismatch; caller ignores result. Existing adaptation calls require declarations, not proof original file must carry handwritten declarations.
items.minimum_option: Unify accessor declarations with actual implementation as a separately approved minimal boundary correction; no speculative return-value behavior.

items.finding: Allocate separate guest GDT/LDT shadows and initialize once
items.evidence: DpmiInit receives original DOSX table in Ldt; allocates two LDT_SIZE arrays, copies GDT and zeroes LDT. Failure clears selector then returns without guest failure result. Reinitialization skips refresh when both addresses nonzero. Original routine only captures Ldt/IntelBase.
items.minimum_option: Resolve table ownership/lifetime and coherent original reuse before retaining allocation/cache; verify repeated initialization and allocation failure.

items.evidence: c_reg.c:1674-1697 setters directly assign LDT state. Current caller uses selector 4 and allocated LDT image. Removing publication alone breaks current consumer connection; this does not prove entire shadow design minimal.
items.minimum_option: Review together with R0135/R0138; retain no standalone second publication route.

counting: Current contiguous adaptation ranges including their comments; excludes #if/#endif and #line scaffolding. Historical anchors were relocated, not used as current counts.
counter_review: Ignoring the setter return does not justify inconsistent declarations, but correcting a declaration is not exact original restoration. Table publication is a real CPU-state dependency; copying/caching and its failure behavior are separate design decisions. Repeated initialization and guest-visible allocation failure have not been demonstrated correct or defective at runtime.
verification: Source review only; no product edits, new build or runtime tests.
